question: Who received the Padma Shri in 2025 for promoting women’s empowerment through Bengali folk percussion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gokul Chandra Das**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gokul Chandra Das** is an acclaimed individual who has been recognized for his contributions to promoting **women’s empowerment** through **Bengali folk percussion.**
 
• He has dedicated his efforts to preserving and popularizing traditional **Bengali folk music**, particularly percussion, as a medium to empower women in rural and urban settings.
 
• His work involved training and mentoring women in percussion techniques, enabling them to gain **financial independence** and social recognition through performances and workshops.
 
• The **Padma Shri**, one of India’s highest civilian honors, was awarded to him in **2025** for his remarkable contributions to cultural promotion and women’s empowerment. This honor highlights his consistent efforts in reviving and sustaining an important aspect of **India’s cultural heritage.**
 
• The recognition of his work signifies the importance of using **art and culture** as tools for **social change** and empowerment, particularly for marginalized groups.
 
• His initiatives have also contributed to the global recognition of **Bengali folk percussion**, showcasing its rich heritage and cultural value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Padma Shri Award:**

 
 
• The **Padma Shri** is the fourth highest civilian award in India, granted for distinguished contributions in various fields such as **arts, education, sports, medicine, social work, public affairs, science, and culture.**
 
• It is awarded annually on **Republic Day** (January 26) by the President of India and aims to recognize individuals who have significantly contributed to their fields and society.
 
 
 
• **Bengali Folk Percussion:**
 
 
• **Bengali folk percussion** is an integral part of **Bengal’s traditional music.** It includes instruments like **dhak, dhol, khol, and tabla.**
 
• These instruments are widely used in festivals, celebrations, and performances across the region.
 
• **Folk percussion** not only serves as a form of entertainment but also acts as a way to preserve and celebrate **cultural heritage.**
 
 
 
• **Women’s Empowerment through Art:**
 
 
• Art and culture have always been powerful tools for **social empowerment**. By training women in percussion, individuals like Gokul Chandra Das have enabled them to gain **confidence** and financial stability.
 
• This empowerment extends beyond financial independence, as it also helps in breaking traditional gender stereotypes.
 
• Women trained in percussion can participate in performances, workshops, and events, showcasing their talent and earning recognition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options:**

 
 
• **Farooq Ahmad Mir:** He is a recognized personality for his contributions in **different fields**, but there is no evidence of his involvement in promoting women’s empowerment through Bengali folk percussion.
 
• **Shyam Bihari Agrawal:** Known for his work in **industrial or economic sectors**, he is not related to this context.
 
• **Sheen Kaaf Nizam:** A notable poet, but his contributions are not aligned with the field of Bengali folk percussion or women’s empowerment through it.
